exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle \left(t-1\right)\left(t^2+2\right) ,\, \ln\left(8-t^2\right) \right\rangle,$ what is $\mathbf r'\left(-1\right)?$
question.explanation:
We differentiate each component separately.

  • For the $x$-component $x(t) = \left(t-1\right)\left(t^2+2\right),$ we have \begin{align} x'(t) & = \left(1\right)\left(t^2+2\right) + \left(t-1\right)\left(2t\right)\\[5pt] & = \left(t^2+2\right) + 2t\left(t-1\right), \end{align} and therefore, \[ x'(-1) = \left(\left(-1\right)^2+2\right) + 2\left(-1\right)\left(\left(-1\right)-1\right) = 7. \]

  • For the $y$-component $y(t) = \ln\left(8-t^2\right),$ we have \[ y'(t) = -\dfrac{2t}{8-t^2}, \] and therefore, \[ y'(-1) = -\dfrac{2\cdot \left(-1\right)}{8-\left(-1\right)^2} = \dfrac{2}{7}. \]

So, we conclude that \begin{align} \mathbf r'\left(-1\right) &= \left\langle x' \left(-1\right), \, y' \left(-1\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{7},\, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{2}{7}}\right\rangle. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle 4e^{2\left(t-1\right)},\, -6\sin\left(t-1\right) \right\rangle,$ what is $\left|\mathbf r'\left(1\right)\right|?$
question.explanation:
We differentiate each component separately.

  • For the $x$-component $x(t) = 4e^{2\left(t-1\right)},$ we have \[ x'(t) = 8e^{2\left(t-1\right)}, \] and therefore, \[ x'\left(1\right) = 8e^{0} = 8. \]

  • For the $y$-component $y(t) =-6\sin\left(t-1\right),$ we have \[ y'(t) = -6\cos\left(t-1\right), \] and therefore, \[ y'\left(1\right) =-6\cos\left(0\right) = -6. \]

So, we conclude that \begin{align} \mathbf r'\left(1\right) &= \left\langle x' \left(1\right), \, y' \left(1\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 8,\, -6\right\rangle. \end{align}

Finally, computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

\begin{align*} \left|\mathbf r'\left(1\right)\right|&= \sqrt{8^2 + \left(-6\right)^2}\\[5pt] &=\sqrt{64 + 36}\\[5pt] & = \sqrt{100}\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle 12\ln(t),\, \dfrac{5}{2}t^2 \right\rangle,$ what is $\left|\mathbf r'\left(2\right)\right|?$ Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
We differentiate each component separately.

  • For the $x$-component $x(t) = 12\ln(t),$ we have \[ x'(t) = \dfrac{12}{t}, \] and therefore, \[ x'\left(2\right) = \dfrac{12}{2} = 6. \]

  • For the $y$-component $y(t) =\dfrac{5}{2}t^2,$ we have \[ y'(t) = 5t, \] and therefore, \[ y'\left(2\right) =5 (2) = 10. \]

So, we conclude that \begin{align} \mathbf r'\left(2\right) &= \left\langle x' \left(2\right), \, y' \left(2\right) \right\rangle \\[5pt] &= \left\langle 6,\, 10\right\rangle. \end{align}

Finally, computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

\begin{align*} \left|\mathbf r'\left(2\right)\right|&= \sqrt{6^2 + 10^2}\\[5pt] &=\sqrt{36 + 100}\\[5pt] & = \sqrt{136}\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2\sqrt{34}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function

question.explanation:
We differentiate each component separately.

  • For the $x$-component $x(t) =e^t-1,$ we have \[ x'(t) = e^t . \]

  • For the $y$-component $y(t) =2\sqrt t,$ we have \[ y'(t) = \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{t}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{t}}. \]

So, we conclude that \begin{align} \mathbf r'\left(t\right) &= \left< x' \left(t\right), \, y' \left(t\right) \right> \\[3pt] &= \left\langle e^t ,\, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{t}}\right\rangle. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \langle \tan 2t,\, te^t\rangle$ what is $\mathbf r'(0)?$
question.explanation:
We differentiate each component separately.

  • For the $x$-component $x(t) = \tan 2t,$ we have \[ x'(t) = 2\sec^2 (2t). \] and therefore, \[ x'(0) = 2\sec^2 0 = 2. \]

  • For the $y$-component $y(t) =te^t,$ we have \[ y'(t) =e^t + te^t = e^t(1+t). \] and therefore, \[ y'(0) = e^0(1+0) = 1. \]

So, we conclude that \begin{align} \mathbf r'\left(0\right) &= \left< x' \left(0\right), \, y' \left(0\right) \right> \\ &= \left\langle 2,\, 1\right\rangle. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: The Derivative of a Three-Component Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Given that  $\mathbf f(t) = \left\langle 4\cos t, \, 3\sin t-t, \, 7t \right\rangle,$   what is $\mathbf f'(\pi)?$
question.explanation:
First, we find $\mathbf f'(t)$ by differentiating each component: \begin{align} \mathbf f'(t) & = \left\langle \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}\bigl(4\cos t\bigr), \, \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}\bigl(3\sin t-t\bigr), \, \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}\bigl(7t\bigr) \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle -4\sin t, \, 3\cos t-1, \, 7 \right\rangle \end{align}

Now, to compute $\mathbf f'(\pi),$ we substitute $t=\pi$ into the expression for $\mathbf f'(t){:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf f'(\pi) & = \left\langle -4\sin(\pi), \, 3\cos(\pi)-1, \, 7 \right\rangle \\[5pt] & = \left\langle \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0}, \, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-4}, \, \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{7} \right\rangle \end{align}

example.title: The Derivative of a Three-Component Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Calculate the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) = \langle \cos t, \: \ln t, \: t^2 \rangle$ with respect to $t.$
question.explanation:
We find the derivative of $\mathbf{f}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f'(t) & = \left\langle \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\cos t), \: \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\ln t), \: \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(t^2) \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle - \sin t, \: \dfrac 1 t, \: 2t \right\rangle \end{align*}

example.title: The Derivative of a Three-Component Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Calculate $\mathbf f'(t)$ given that $\mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} e^{t+1} \\ \cos t \\ \sqrt{t} \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
We find $\mathbf{f}'(t)$ by differentiating each component:

\begin{align*} \mathbf f'(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (e^{t+1}) \\ \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\cos t) \\ \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\sqrt{t}) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} e^{t+1} \\ -\sin{t} \\ \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{t}} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

example.title: The Derivative of a Three-Component Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) = \begin{bmatrix} t^2+3t \\ \ln{t} \\ \sin{\pi t} \end{bmatrix}$ at $t=1.$
question.explanation:
First, we find $\mathbf{f}'(t)$ by differentiating each component: \begin{align*} \mathbf f'(t) & = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (t^2+3t) \\ \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\ln{t}) \\ \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (\sin{\pi t}) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2t+3 \\ \dfrac{1}{t} \\ \pi \cos{\pi t} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Now, to compute $\mathbf f'(1)$ we substitute $t=1$ into the expression for $\mathbf f'(t){:}$ \begin{align} \mathbf f(1) & = \begin{bmatrix} 2(1)+3 \\ \dfrac{1}{1} \\ \pi \cos(\pi\cdot 1) \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 2+3 \\ 1 \\ \pi \cos{\pi} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \\ -\pi \end{bmatrix} \end{align}

question.text: Calculate the derivative of $\mathbf f(t) = \langle \arctan 4t, 6(t+5)^2 , 14-t \rangle$ with respect to $t.$
question.explanation:
We find the derivative of $\mathbf{f}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

\begin{align} \mathbf f'(t) & = \left\langle \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\arctan 4t), \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(6(t+5)^2) , \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(14-t) \right\rangle \\[3pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac 4 {1+16t^2}, 12t +60 , -1 \right\rangle \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: The Second Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \langle t^2 + \cos t ,\, t\sin (t) \rangle,$ $\mathbf r''(t)=$
question.explanation:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

  • For $x(t) = t^2+ \cos t ,$ we have \begin{align} x'(t) &= 2t -\sin t\\[3pt] x''(t) &= 2-\cos t . \end{align}

  • For $y(t) = t\sin t,$ we have \begin{align*} y'(t) &= \sin t + t\cos t\\[3pt] y''(t) &= \cos t + \cos t -t\sin t\\[3pt] & = 2\cos t -t\sin t. \end{align*}

So, we conclude that \begin{align} \mathbf{r}''(t) &= \left< x''(t), \, y''(t) \right> \\[3pt] & = \left\langle 2-\cos t,\, 2\cos t-t\sin t\right\rangle. \end{align}

question.text: Find the second derivative of $\mathbf f(t) = 2\ln{t} \, \mathbf i - (\cos t + e^t) \, \mathbf j + (2t^3+ t -2) \, \mathbf k$ with respect to $t.$
question.explanation:
First, we find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

\begin{align} \mathbf f'(t) & = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(2\ln{t}) \, \mathbf i - \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\cos t +e^t) \, \mathbf j + \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (2t^3 + t -2) \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{t} \, \mathbf i - ( -\sin t +e^t) \, \mathbf j + (6t^2 +1)\, \mathbf k\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{2}{t} \, \mathbf i + ( \sin t - e^t) \, \mathbf j +(6t^2 + 1)\, \mathbf k \end{align}

Then, we calculate $\mathbf{f}''(t)$ by differentiating $\mathbf f'(t)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf f''(t) & = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}\left( \dfrac{2}{t} \right) \, \mathbf i + \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}( \sin t - e^t) \, \mathbf j+ \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(6t^2 + 1) \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{2}{t^2} \, \mathbf i + (\cos t- e^t) \, \mathbf j + 12t\, \mathbf k \end{align}

question.explanation:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

  • For $x(t) = \dfrac{t}{t-1},$ we have \begin{align} x'(t) &=\dfrac{(t-1)-t}{(t-1)^2}\\[3pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{(t-1)^2}\\[3pt] x''(t) & = \dfrac{2}{(t-1)^3}. \end{align}

  • For $y(t) = \sin(2t),$ we have \begin{align*} y'(t) &= 2\cos(2t)\\[3pt] y''(t) &= -4\sin(2t). \end{align*}

So, we conclude that \begin{align} \mathbf{r}''(t) &= \left< x''(t), \, y''(t) \right> \\[3pt] & = \left\langle \dfrac{2}{(t-1)^3},\, -4\sin(2t)\right\rangle. \end{align}

question.text: Find the second derivative of $\mathbf f(t) = 2t^3 \, \mathbf i - (\cos t +t^2) \, \mathbf j + (5t^3+ \sqrt5 t -2\sqrt5) \, \mathbf k$ with respect to $t.$
question.explanation:
First, we find the derivative of $\mathbf f(t)$ by differentiating each component.

\begin{align} \mathbf f'(t) & = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(2t^3) \, \mathbf i - \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(\cos t +t^2) \, \mathbf j + \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt} (5t^3+ \sqrt5 t -2\sqrt5) \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] & = 6t^2 \, \mathbf i - ( - \sin t +2t) \, \mathbf j +(15t^2 + \sqrt 5)\, \mathbf k\\[5pt] & = 6t^2 \, \mathbf i + ( \sin t -2t) \, \mathbf j +(15t^2 + \sqrt 5)\, \mathbf k \end{align}

Then, we calculate $\mathbf{f}''(t)$ by differentiating $\mathbf f'(t)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align} \mathbf f''(t) & = \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}( 6t^2) \, \mathbf i + \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}( \sin t -2t) \, \mathbf j+ \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm dt}(15t^2 + \sqrt 5) \, \mathbf k \\[5pt] & = 12t \, \mathbf i + (\cos t- 2) \, \mathbf j +30t\, \mathbf k \end{align}
